name: CO-02
label: Safe D

key_factors: District leans about 20 points Democratic, structurally favoring the incumbent party
Neguse has raised $2.7M with $3.1M on hand; Dennison reports no fundraising
Prediction markets price Neguse's reelection near 96-98%

model.rationale: Neguse combines incumbency, a large financial edge, and a district that leans 20 points Democratic, while his challenger has shown no measurable fundraising. Prediction markets and district fundamentals align on a comfortable double-digit win, so the seat stays Safe Democratic.
model.watch: Only an extraordinary national wave against Democrats or an unforeseen scandal could shrink the margin, and even that would be unlikely to threaten the seat itself.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.

overview:
Colorado's 2nd District is firmly Democratic territory, with a partisan lean of roughly 20 points toward the party. Joe Neguse, the incumbent, is seeking another term and enters the general election with a commanding financial position: about $2.7 million raised this cycle and more than $3 million in the bank. His Republican opponent, Kelley Dennison, reports no fundraising figures, and Libertarian Gaylon Kent is also on the ballot.

No public general-election polls or expert ratings are available for this race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals, the money gap, and prediction markets, which price Neguse's chances at roughly 96 percent or higher. With a well-funded, established incumbent in a heavily Democratic seat, the race is rated Safe Democratic with an expected margin in the mid-20s. The real question is the size of the victory, not who wins.
